narrative: 把人物放在十字准星上，整个图式就会随之改变。偏离中心的空间不再属于视线朝外的意图。
两侧剩余的场域变成了对等的侍从。主体拥有这条轴线，
其他一切都归属于两翼。当角色应当处于搜寻、逃亡或偷听状态时，这就不是对的工具。
把人群中的一个间谍强行居中，会把他变成一张海报。而把一位神明、一个身着戏服的孩子、一个独裁者，或一个喜剧式的木讷角色强行居中，则能让这种形式感变得清晰可读。
你完全可以在一个凌乱的房间里把一张脸强行居中，那依然算是正中取景。
建筑本身不必对此致敬。如果整个房间都在致敬，你其实已经走进了中心构图，甚至可能是对称构图的领域。
how: 让镜头轴线对齐胸骨或鼻梁。除非你想要一种笑点或威胁感，否则应保持竖直线条不倾斜。
较长的镜头（65mm到85mm）能孤立出这个靶心。较广的镜头则能展现房间本身是否也呈轴线对称。
检查两侧耳朵旁边的剩余空间是否相当，再决定这种对等本身是否就是重点。提示词：Central framing of [Subject], the figure on the optical axis, bilateral weight, a formal altar in the frame.
when: 当一个角色必须被呈现、被审判，或被膜拜时使用它：穿过门廊的登场、一张正式的肖像、一次望向镜头的喜剧凝视。不要把它用在一次需要在视线前方留出空气感的场景中。
vs: 中心构图（Centered Composition）把整个画面场域都围绕轴线组织起来，常常呈现为一幅正面活人画。正中取景则可以只是身体位于十字准星上。
对称构图（Symmetry）让质量互为镜像。你完全可以在一条非对称的街道正中央强行放置一张脸。
三分法（Rule of Thirds）是你正在打破的默认规则。单点透视（One-Point Perspective）会在同一条轴线上加入一个消失点。
examples_film: 《布达佩斯大饭店》（The Grand Budapest Hotel）把门房和客人强行居中，仿佛他们是一枚枚邮票；《月升王国》（Moonrise Kingdom）对穿着制服的孩子们也如法炮制，正面而毫不羞怯。
这种形式感既是笑点，也是温柔。这是语法，而不是韦斯·安德森的一套服装道具。
mistakes: 最常见的误用是带着一点懒散偏移的三分法构图。破绽是视线一侧留白比头后方更多。
修正方法：把人物滑动到两侧剩余空间相等的位置，或者承认你想要的其实是前导空间（Lead Room），并保留这种偏移。

faq.q: 电影中的正中取景（Central Framing）是什么？
faq.a: 它是把人物精确放置在光学轴线上的做法，一次“正中强击”。身体位于十字准星之上。两侧剩余的空间是对等的。人物是被呈现出来的，而不是嵌入某个三分点。

faq.q: 正中取景（Central Framing）与中心构图（Centered Composition）有何区别？
faq.a: 正中取景关乎身体所在的位置：在轴线上。中心构图则是整个图式：家具、墙壁和其他人物往往也一同加入这座祭坛。你可以在一个凌乱的房间里把一张脸强行居中，那是没有完整居中活人画的正中取景。

faq.q: 什么时候该用正中取景（Central Framing）？
faq.a: 用它来呈现、评判或调侃：一次正式的登场、一张肖像、一个穿制服的孩子、一个坐在办公桌前的暴君。不要在视线需要空间感，或角色应当感觉像是别人画面中的客人时使用它。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写正中取景（Central Framing）的提示词？
faq.a: 说明“正中”和“光学轴线”。示例：Central framing of [Subject], the figure on the optical axis, bilateral weight, a formal altar in the frame。加上“摄影机对齐”。如果你只写“肖像”，得到的只会是三分法构图。

narrative: Put them on the crosshairs and the diagram changes. Off-center space no longer belongs to the look.
Both leftover fields become equal attendants. The subject owns the axis.
Everyone else owns the wings. It is the wrong tool when the character should be hunting, fleeing, or eavesdropping.
A center punch on a spy in a crowd makes them a poster. A center punch on a god, a child in costume, a dictator, or a comic stiff makes the formality legible.
You can center-punch a face in a messy room. That is still central framing.
The architecture does not have to salute. If the whole room salutes, you have walked into centered composition and maybe into symmetry.
how: Align the lens axis with the sternum or the bridge of the nose. Keep verticals upright unless you want a joke or a threat.
A longer lens (65mm to 85mm) isolates the bullseye. A wider lens will show whether the room is also axial.
Check both ears have similar leftover, then decide if that equality is the point. Prompt: Central framing of [Subject], the figure on the optical axis, bilateral weight, a formal altar in the frame.
when: Use it when a character must be presented, judged, or worshipped: an arrival through doors, a formal portrait, a comic stare into lens. Do not use it on a look-off that needs air in front of the eyes.
vs: Centered Composition organizes the entire field around the axis, often as a frontal tableau. Central framing can be just the body on the crosshairs.
Symmetry mirrors masses. You can punch a face dead center in an asymmetric street.
Rule of Thirds is the default you are breaking. One-Point Perspective adds a vanishing point on that same axis.
examples_film: The Grand Budapest Hotel center-punches concierges and guests as if they were stamps. Moonrise Kingdom does the same with children in uniform, frontal and unembarrassed.
The formality is the joke and the tenderness. Grammar, not a Wes Anderson costume kit.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is thirds with a slightly lazy offset. The tell is more air on the look side than behind the head.
The fix is to slide the figure until both leftover fields match, or to admit you wanted Lead Room and keep the offset.

faq.q: What is central framing in film?
faq.a: It is dead-center placement of the figure on the optical axis, a center punch. The body sits on the crosshairs. Leftover space on both sides is equal. The person is presented, not nested into a third.

Central framing is where the body sits: on the axis. Centered composition is the whole diagram: furniture, walls, and other bodies often join the altar. You can center-punch a face in a messy room. That is central framing without a full centered tableau.

faq.q: When should I use central framing?
faq.a: Use it to present, judge, or joke: a formal arrival, a portrait, a child in a uniform, a tyrant at a desk. Do not use it when the look needs air, or when the character should feel like a guest in someone else's frame.

faq.q: How do I prompt central framing for AI image or video?
faq.a: Say dead center and optical axis. Example: Central framing of [Subject], the figure on the optical axis, bilateral weight, a formal altar in the frame. Add square to camera. If you only write portrait, you will get thirds.
